questions.q: What is the core revenue recognition principle?
options: Revenue is recognized whenever cash is received, regardless of delivery
Revenue is recognized only at the end of the fiscal year
Revenue is recognized when control of a good or service transfers to the customer, in the amount the business expects to be entitled to receive
Revenue is recognized before any contract is signed
questions.explain: The core principle ties revenue recognition to the transfer of control, not to the timing of cash.

questions.q: In the simplified five-step model, what comes immediately after identifying the contract?
options: Identifying the separate performance obligations within the contract
Recognizing all revenue immediately
Collecting payment from the customer
Closing the accounting period
questions.explain: Step 2 is identifying the distinct performance obligations (separate promises) within the contract.

questions.q: Thistledown Systems sells a $12,000 package: a $9,000 license delivered immediately and $3,000 of support over 12 months. How much revenue is recognized at the moment of delivery?
options: $12,000, the full contract amount
$9,000, the license's standalone value
$3,000, the support value
$0, since no cash was collected yet
questions.explain: The license is delivered immediately, so its $9,000 standalone value is recognized at delivery; the $3,000 of support is recognized over the following 12 months.

questions.q: Why can't a bundled contract (software + support + hardware) typically be recognized as 'all revenue, all at once'?
options: Because bundled contracts are illegal
Because bundled contracts never generate any revenue
Because only hardware generates revenue, never services
Because each component may be a separate performance obligation delivered at a different time, requiring the price to be allocated and recognized accordingly
questions.explain: Different components of a bundled contract are often separate performance obligations, each recognized as its own obligation is satisfied.

questions.q: Why is revenue recognition one of the most heavily regulated areas of accounting?
options: Because it has no real effect on a company's reported financial performance
Because it only applies to government contracts
Because getting it wrong, intentionally or not, directly misstates a company's reported performance
Because revenue recognition rules change every single month
questions.explain: Since revenue recognition timing directly affects reported financial results, it is carefully governed by standards like ASC 606 and IFRS 15.
